Hi Ella — great data, thanks for sharing. High-level thoughts below and then two concrete packaging options you can present to procurement.

Quick summary of how we handle these patterns: we support (a) time-limited step-downs with prorated credits, (b) burst credits that you pre-purchase and only draw when needed, and (c) an "elastic annual" that combines a smaller committed baseline + larger burst allotment for predictable unit pricing.

Option A — Offseason Lite (monthly, flexible)
- Keep current hosted model, move to a lower baseline tier for Jul–Sep (prorated monthly).
- Embeddings as an add-on billed per 1k vectors; include the reranking plugin as an included entitlement for the pilot period.
- No early-termination penalties; switching back to higher tier is immediate but subject to provisioning lead time (~24 hours).
- Estimated: ~42% bill reduction Jul–Sep vs current run-rate (rough estimate based on usage file).

Option B — Annual Flex (recommended if you want predictable unit cost)
- 12-month commitment with a lower per-token rate and a 15% surge credit pool included (usable any time).
- Embeddings bundled (flat per-embedding unit) if you commit at >= 500k vectors/mo average; reranking plugin included at the enterprise addon level.
- Yearly pricing includes 1x emergency scale window and rollover of up to 20% unused credits into next quarter.
- Estimated: ~30% lower effective unit cost vs month-to-month; requires annual billing/commit.

Ask for procurement: Which is higher priority — the absolute lowest unit cost (lean toward Option B) or max short-term flexibility (Option A). If they want both we can do a hybrid: 6-month baseline with an annual discount applied to the next 6 months if you convert.

Icc: Ben and Karthik — Ben, can you add a short note about embedding bundling technical implications (latency, caching) for Ella? Karthik, can you draft the quote matrix for the two options and include proration / rollback language?

If it helps, I'm free Tue/Wed for a 30-min procurement walkthrough.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Hi Ella — quick technical note to supplement Irene's commercial options.

- Embeddings bundled with the API vs as a standalone endpoint: bundling reduces orchestration overhead and simplifies billing, but keep in mind that embedding-heavy pipelines with different sequence lengths can increase tail latency if routed to the same worker pools. We typically recommend a small dedicated pool for embeddings if you have >200k vectors/month.
- Caching: prefix / KV-cache for common prompts (diagnostic triage templates) can shave 20–35% of token cost on repeated queries. We can help set conservative TTLs for your use case.
- Reranking plugin: works as a post-process step; cheap in compute but benefits from cached embeddings. Bundling it as an entitlement makes the UX simpler and keeps latency predictable.

I've attached a short playbook that shows cost/latency tradeoffs and sample configurations for the two packaging options. Happy to walk through the configs on a call.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
